Two prisoners meet across the fence in the orbital detention yard.

Oz and K exchange names through the vents between their cells.
The dogs find a route through the detention block.

Oz and Felicia listen as Mike and K compare names and memories.

At Waldo’s house, the capsule beacon predates the station intake. Felicia identifies the cassette hiss. K taps a drum pad after the tape stops, and Waldo hears his live beat.
Mike traces the quiet channel as the team considers the cost of leaving.
K holds the embroidered K patch and keeps his chosen name.
At Waldo’s home workbench, Felicia identifies the local relay and K keeps his chosen name on its record. The group heads outside past the porch.
At Waldo’s house, the team connects an isolated reader to Orpheus. A voice answers.
The shift calls Waldo’s house to weigh shutdown, central control and an open network.
The team writes down its decision to open the network and name its owners.
The feed goes quiet and local protection takes over.
The first morning brings a ticket for human review.
Mike returns to the maintenance queue and checks the first label.

Officers enter the Ghost Bends performance and confront Red.
Red gives Iona his car keys and tells her to go.
Iona blinds the camera, races past the fence and climbs into the coupe.

Iona drives toward daylight listening to Somewhere Deep Down Below.

Iona stops the car by the water as morning breaks.
Aboard the transport, Red works himself free of the restraints.
Red makes his way through the transport to the control room.

Orbital custody processes Red at intake.
The detainee’s skills are retained while his memory is conditioned.
Alone in the cell, K tries the door controls.
In a Low Quarter recollection, Red and Iona share work across the bench.
Iona counts the band in and Ghost Bends takes the stage.

Iona keeps a set list while Red heads toward the relay vault.
Red opens the way through the vault as the machinery fails.
Red and Iona confront the cost of the door he opened.

Iona asks Red what he wants and hands him a guitar.
Red works at the bench and remembers the choice that brought him there.

K retrieves his belongings and attempts another escape.
The escape brings K back to the bunk in cell 118.
K listens to the hum behind the cell vent.
Life in the Low Quarter continues at the workbench and on the Ghost Bends stage.
The walls of cell 118 open onto an unfamiliar, luminous landscape.
K shares tea with Buddha and recognizes something familiar.
K receives a ceremonial robe and a pale mask.
During the ascent, K wears the ivory mask and lifts it away. Under the green-and-gold hood his dark eyes show through square glasses. He recognizes his own face and says “El.”
Back in Cell 118, K listens at the vent. He keeps the face he saw beneath the mask, even as the words of the encounter slip away.
